infosec.title: Critical Apache Roller RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation, No Authentication Required
infosec.summary: Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 have an unauthenticated deserialization flaw in the XML-RPC endpoint that allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code. It is being actively exploited. Users should upgrade to Roller 6.1.6 or later. If patching is delayed, set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml, remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping, and restart Roller. Disabling XML-RPC in the admin UI does not prevent exploitation on older versions.

infosec.title: PHP Fixes 7 Critical Flaws, Including Bugs That Could Allow Remote Code Execution
infosec.summary: Following a preemptive notice, the PHP Foundation released a security advisory and updates to fix seven critical vulnerabilities. Depthfirst codenamed one of the vulnerabilities phpAfterShell and developed a PoC that demonstrated how it can be exploited to create an arbitrary deserialization primitive which, when chained with another deserialization-to-RCE vulnerability, can lead to arbitrary code execution. The vulnerability affects any application that runs an affected PHP version with file-based sessions.

infosec.title: Security Logging in Cloud Environments - Kubernetes
infosec.summary: Marco Lancini outlines the various log sources that are available for Kubernetes environments and their uses. Lancini also highlights blind spots such as events from on the node, API events that are sent directly to the kubelet instead of via the API server, and events from within a kubetctl exec shell. The post concludes by walking through a practical setup.

infosec.title: EggStreme Malware: Rebuilt Under Scrutiny
infosec.summary: Bitdefender reports that the EggStreme operators rebuilt Fuel, Loader, and Agent after its September 2025 disclosure. Fuel now uses AES-256-CBC encryption for its configuration. Loader payloads use RC5 or custom CBC ciphers. Agent traffic moved from gRPC to raw TCP over mutual TLS, with AES-256-CBC added. New commands enumerate Active Directory users, groups, and servers, run WMI with supplied credentials, impersonate user tokens, load .NET assemblies, and run PowerShell in memory. Some builds listen on TCP 5060 and add a firewall rule named “Core Networking - SIP.” The operators moved toward campaign-specific certificate authorities. Bitdefender assesses with high confidence that Philippine government organizations remain targets, with multiple victims; it assesses Taiwan targeting at low to medium confidence.

product.title: Planning an AI feature people will actually use
product.summary: This practical framework plans AI features by targeting specific user friction points rather than deploying generic chatbots. Teams should map value against risk and write capability briefs before prototyping.

product.title: 6 Ways to deliver value before the paywall and settle the paywall placement debate
product.summary: The paywall placement debate stems from unclear definitions of user value. This post shares six ways apps can deliver pre-paywall value effectively.

product.title: When the Boss Starts Shipping: Product Leaders, AI and the Codebase
product.summary: When leaders use AI tools to ship code directly to production, it creates hidden tech debt. Establishing separate sandbox and production lanes ensures leadership follows standard testing processes.

product.summary: AI PM work should be structured around explicit decision rights rather than routine tasks.

product.title: Friction worth protecting when shaping products
product.summary: While AI automates intent friction, teams must preserve "problem friction" - the hard work of exploring user needs.

design.title: Canva Now Lets Users Turn Off Generative AI Features
design.summary: Canva has introduced settings that let free and paid users disable generative AI tools, including Magic Write, Magic Design, Magic Edit, Dream Lab, and Canva Code. Non-generative features such as Background Remover and Magic Grab remain available because they manipulate existing content rather than create new material. A separate preference reduces AI-generated templates and graphics in search results, prioritizing human-created content without guaranteeing that AI material disappears entirely.

design.title: Big Changes to the Adobe Fonts Website
design.summary: Adobe Fonts' biggest website upgrade in years merges search and browsing into one interface that filters 36,000 fonts by OpenType features and variable axes. A new AI recommendation page suggests fonts matching the mood of uploaded inspiration images, even ones without any text. Family pages now also show glyph maps and illustrated OpenType feature breakdowns.

design.title: Docker Rebrand 2026: New Logo, Colors, and Strategy Explained
design.summary: Docker has introduced a new visual identity and the positioning "Run on Trust," reflecting its expansion from application containers toward secure execution environments for autonomous AI agents. The redesign simplifies its recognizable whale logo into a containment-inspired symbol, replaces Docker Blue with a more violet-toned blue, and introduces GT Planar and GT Standard Mono typography. A darker website and expanded color palette accompany the strategic shift, positioning Docker as infrastructure for safely running both traditional applications and AI agents.

design.title: Should You Actually Add AI to That? A Four-Question Audit for Product Teams
design.summary: Adding AI helps only when what it returns in saved effort, caught errors, or consistency outweighs what users spend learning and verifying it. This post presents a four-question audit that asks whether the feature cuts total effort, beats the current method, lets users catch errors, and preserves verification skills after a year. A benefits-appeals tool became worthwhile once rescoped from drafting determinations to surfacing relevant provisions.

design.title: It's official: creatives are using AI daily, but most aren't making extra money from it
design.summary: Envato's survey of 1,033 creatives across 103 countries found that 87% use AI at work and 58% use it daily, although increased productivity rarely translates into higher earnings. Among creatives who report working faster with AI, only one in four see a financial benefit, while 53% of AI users have used AI on important client work without disclosing it. Taste and judgment ranked as the most valuable skills at 53%, followed by craft at 49%, while prompting fell to last place among eight skills at 19%.

design.title: Design by Playground
design.summary: AI coding agents are making it practical for designers to create temporary, purpose-built design tools instead of relying exclusively on general-purpose applications like Figma. These interactive playgrounds let designers manipulate variables, compare alternatives, and test real content, animation, loading states, and edge cases directly in the environment where the software will run. Agents can build them in minutes, so playgrounds can be created for individual design questions and discarded afterward, with successful decisions exported as code or design tokens.

design.summary: Talk through the critique, the handoff notes or the Figma Make prompt the way you'd explain it at the whiteboard. design.summary: An encyclopedia written by a deliberating panel of models: blind ledgers, cross-examination, lot-drawn juries, and a bias report.

design.summary: Nameshot gives every new screenshot a proper name, right on your Mac.

design.title: The Multiplier Effect: How Authoring Tools Can Transform Web Accessibility
design.summary: Website builders and content management systems could multiply web accessibility by prompting for alt text and offering only WCAG-conforming options. With 74% of new web pages in April 2025 containing AI-generated content, well-designed AI could improve accessibility while poor implementations multiply barriers. W3C is updating its decade-old Authoring Tool Accessibility Guidelines and invites anyone interested to join the ATAG Community Group.

design.title: Omoi's identity for Eclipse Space looks back to the Apollo program
design.summary: Stockholm-based Omoi has developed an identity for satellite infrastructure company Eclipse Space inspired by the optimism, engineering, and visual language of NASA's Apollo program. The system combines a custom Eclipse Space Display typeface, Gorton-inspired interface labels, vibrant space-themed colors, and interactive website buttons modeled on the Apollo Guidance Computer's physical keys. Its distinctive solar corona symbol is generated through a custom tool developed with Claude Code, producing unique variations that follow consistent visual rules and reinforce the company's positioning around independent ownership of satellite networks.

design.title: This non-alcoholic aperitif packaging was made with real plants, sunlight, and embossed glass
design.summary: LOVE. has refreshed the identity and packaging of non-alcoholic aperitif Everleaf, combining sustainable glassmaking with botanical illustrations created through traditional cyanotype photography. The redesigned bottles use 100% post-consumer recycled glass, weigh 23% less than their predecessors, and feature embossed acacia leaves alongside a refined wordmark. Real plants exposed onto light-sensitive paper produce distinctive illustrations for the Forest, Mountain, and Marine varieties, connecting each product's ingredients to its visual identity.

design.title: More Liquid Glass refinements being tested in iOS 27.3 beta
design.summary: Apple is testing a subtler Liquid Glass effect in iOS 27.3 that restores the softer fading of scrolling content beneath navigation bars.

design.title: Does NVIDIA Need a New Logo as Well as a New CEO?
design.summary: After Jensen Huang's resignation, NVIDIA's 2006 logo, with its wonky eye and lime-green palette, looks ripe for a careful evolution that keeps two decades of recognition.

design.title: Suno Now Lets You Make AI Videos for Your AI Music
design.summary: Suno's new Visuals feature generates images and 15-second videos that sync automatically with its AI songs, including lipsynced lyrics, on web, iOS, and Android.

marketing.title: What winning direct mail campaigns get right
marketing.summary: This year's Postmark Award winners are raising the bar in direct mail, and so we turned their best ideas into a playbook ! We pulled practical strategies from L'Occitane, SimpliSafe, Ramp, and other brands so that you can bring the same thinking to your own program. Now you can: >>Design mailpieces that earn a second look >>Personalize from end-to-end by getting smarter with customer data >>Connect direct mail with email and SMS in your journeys >>Scale your program to new audiences Get the playbook →

marketing.title: Tech outages are causing people to panic-buy
marketing.summary: Recent tech outages across Microsoft, US airlines, and JPMorgan are driving consumers to stock up on emergency supplies. Costco is benefiting, with US comparable sales rising an estimated 11% to 12% in the final week of October compared with its typical 6% to 7% growth. Momentum continued into November as 21 of 26 generators tracked on Costco's website sold out. Sam's Club and home improvement retailers are also seeing increased demand.

marketing.title: Brands are hiring former journalists for storytelling. Or are they?
marketing.summary: More brands are hiring former journalists as storytellers, often to produce the original-data stories and service pieces that AI search tends to cite. More than 2,800 journalists have moved into brand editorial roles over the past decade. However, many hiring managers still default to candidates with linear marketing careers, and former editors with brand experience tend to win out over reporters.

marketing.title: How Brands Are Going Viral With Advent Calendars
marketing.summary: Beauty and CPG brands are filling TikTok feeds with advent calendars before Black Friday, since one box can fuel weeks of unboxings and debates when each door gives people a reason to keep watching. Burger King releases only 110 calendars a day, so fans follow the drop before the doors even open. Red Bull added one pack-exclusive flavor that has fans debating whether to buy the whole box for it.

marketing.title: Make Them Type the Promo Code: Why a Little Effort Beats an Automatic Discount in Digital Shopping
marketing.summary: Requiring customers to enter a promo code can generate more sales than automatically applying the same discount. A study found that a 15% discount redeemed through a promo code converted at 1.45%, compared with 0.91% for an automatic discount. The small action makes customers feel like they earned the deal, increasing their sense of value and likelihood of redeeming it. The tactic works best for modest discounts of 10% to 15%, but the effort should remain minimal. Additional steps can create frustration and eliminate the benefit.

marketing.title: When influencers post sponsored content, your brand should...
marketing.summary: Your brand should actively support influencer content after it goes live rather than leaving all the engagement to creators. Have your social team comment on sponsored posts, reply to every comment, involve public-facing employees, share posts to Instagram Stories, and use reposts and tagged content to feature creator posts on your brand profile. For campaigns with multiple influencers, send creators links to each other's posts and encourage them to engage. Discuss these tactics with creators beforehand so everyone understands their role in promoting the partnership.

marketing.title: Who should pay for a franchisee's website?
marketing.summary: If you market through dealers, franchisees or agents, the budget usually exists already, spread across local agencies and freelancers. Wix Enterprise's Partner Website Blueprint covers three funding models , what corporate should control versus leave to locals, and how One network replaced 192 chapter sites in three days. Read the blueprint →

marketing.title: agentic-pmm Claude Skills
marketing.summary: Join the waitlist to get access to a free library of Claude skills for product marketers. The skills cover product positioning, GTM readiness, competitor tracking, and more. The library will become available to waitlist members on December 14.

marketing.title: Google Deep Review
marketing.summary: Deep Review is an agentic AI system from Google Research that checks technical, scientific, and business documents for errors, inconsistencies, and weak claims. It supports PDFs and plain text. The tool provides two free document reviews per week.

marketing.title: Agentic Shopping - Maybe Nobody Wants This
marketing.summary: Agentic shopping faces consumer trust barriers as shoppers remain hesitant to let AI agents spend their money. While AI is used to research and compare products, retailers want to retain control of the actual purchase and customer relationship. Catalyst Brands is investing in loyalty programs to strengthen direct customer relationships across brands like JC Penney and Brooks Brothers.

marketing.title: PayPal Said Honey Followed Last-Click Attribution, Which Was the Whole Problem
marketing.summary: Last-click attribution can overstate the performance of advertising channels that capture sales rather than generate them. This is especially common in brand search, retargeting, coupon extensions, cart abandonment emails, and affiliate marketing. A 2015 eBay study found that turning off paid search ads had no significant impact on sales, even though attribution reports credited those ads with strong returns. Run incrementality tests to measure actual sales lift, exclude brand searches from automated campaigns, and revise affiliate terms to limit commissions for partners that only capture credit at checkout.

marketing.title: Sam Altman warns against a future where AI, not humans, calls the shots
marketing.summary: Sam Altman and Greg Brockman oppose the idea of gradually handing control of society to AI as models become more powerful. Both believe humans must remain in charge but differ on how to prevent an accidental or intentional handover. Brockman stressed the growing need for better AI monitoring and security as models become harder to track through traditional chain-of-thought monitoring. Following a security breach, OpenAI redirected 25% of production engineers to security work.

marketing.title: Product Marketing Explained (2 minute video)
marketing.summary: An overview of product marketing and how PMMs drive research, positioning, GTM strategy, and enablement.

marketing.title: Over half of adult Americans are gamers
marketing.summary: More than half of Americans aged 16-69 play video games weekly and spend over 2B minutes a day gaming on TV.

marketing.title: TikTok Outpaces Instagram on Brand Engagement Despite Equal Reach
marketing.summary: TikTok turns the same reach into more engagement and faster follower growth, while Instagram Reels still lead every format on shares.

founders.title: 78% of finance leaders think customers would trust AI to apply for credit. Only 34% of customers agree
founders.summary: When your entire day is AI, it's easy to forget that not everyone's on the same page - especially when it comes to personal finance. Plaid and The Harris Poll surveyed 1,002 financial services decision-makers, then checked their assumptions against 2,002 U.S. consumers . ⚠️ Leaders consistently overestimated how comfortable customers are with AI - especially when it comes to AI making decisions without human oversight. Plaid's State of Intelligent Finance: Fall 2026 report covers: Where the trust gap is widest, and how to close it How to set limits as AI starts taking action Who should answer for AI's mistakes Download the free report

founders.title: Introducing the Stripe AI Index
founders.summary: Founders have been guessing how much real revenue sits behind the AI boom. Stripe launched a weekly AI Index tracking payments to about 20,000 AI businesses on its platform. Aggregate AI revenue rose 103% over the past year and easily beat the SaaS Index. Median AI growth trailed aggregate growth by a wide margin, so larger AI companies appear to be doing better than typical ones. The index only counts payments through Stripe and tracks weekly shifts as overall growth cools.

founders.title: The new App Store nobody's optimizing for
founders.summary: Apps can now integrate with ChatGPT, allowing interactions without leaving the chat, as seen with partners like Spotify and Expedia. Developers can seize this low-friction distribution channel, ensuring app functions complete quickly and drive users back to their main platform. However, reliance on ChatGPT means limited control over distribution, possible cuts of transactions by OpenAI, and user relationships residing in the chat interface.

founders.title: Your Next GTM Hire Should Be a Creative Marketer.
founders.summary: Cold email volume has exploded now that anyone can launch a massive campaign in minutes with Claude Code. About 91% of cold emails get no replies. A B2B outbound agency reports lifting its reply rate to 15% by targeting signals like a fresh funding round or a new sales leader. Everyone can automate the sending now, so the next hire after a GTM engineer should be a creative marketer who owns the angle and the copy. Teams should score that marketer on replies and message tests.

founders.title: Employee-led content programs are a dangerously good distribution strategy
founders.summary: Employee-led content programs create a ripple effect that can bring any company exponential upside. This post presents a guide on how anyone can get started. What kills these programs are copy-paste captions, forced posting quotas, and posts that only promote the company. People can smell a mandate.

founders.title: How did Lovable grow so fast?
founders.summary: Most founders look for a secret growth playbook behind breakout startups. Lovable turned two this week with over $600 million in annual recurring revenue and no growth hack. The AI app builder rides an exploding category, so tactics that failed at older software companies now work like a raft on a fast river. The lean team ships big updates nearly every week to keep word of mouth moving. New hires are expected to automate the repetitive parts of their own jobs with AI from the start.

founders.title: Your business moves fast. So should your money.
founders.summary: Your business moves quickly. Your money should, too. Stripe Treasury brings payments and financial tools together, helping you pay vendors, send payouts, issue cards, and manage cash flow with less complexity. Build more efficient financial operations on the same platform your business already uses for payments as you continue growing. See how it works

founders.title: Building the next generation of automated bidding at Microsoft Advertising
founders.summary: Microsoft Advertising is automatically rolling out updated bidding models that adjust nearly twice as fast after target changes. Advertisers on Maximize Conversion Value or Target ROAS see 10% more conversion value per click at similar return, provided they have working conversion tracking with real transaction values.

founders.title: Become a founding member of TLDR's AI community (2 minute form)
founders.summary: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join .

founders.title: Vercel Billing CLI
founders.summary: Vercel now groups every billing command under vercel billing in its CLI, covering usage, contracts, and budgets. Teams can check their plan, billing cycle, and balance due, download past invoices, and preview upcoming charges without opening the dashboard. Billing overview and invoice history work on all plans under existing permissions, while upcoming invoice estimates require a paid subscription.

founders.title: The M&A Process | Who, What, and When
founders.summary: Most founders only see the public announcement of an acquisition and rarely hear how messy the private process gets. Company sales start with only top executives and the board in the loop because leaks distract employees and weaken the seller's hand. Choosing an investment bank is a common leak point since banks that lose the pitch often talk. Many deals die early in the process, so keeping the circle tight avoids spooking customers unnecessarily. Bankers and lawyers also cost more than most founders expect.

founders.title: How I used AI to get 25 million views in 7 weeks
founders.summary: Founders often let their social accounts go quiet once daily work takes over. A dormant Threads account reached 25 million views across platforms after an AI loop began drafting new posts from old hit ideas. Raw views converted into far fewer followers on Threads than on Instagram, so select posts offered a free guide and collected 1,745 email addresses. The system scores core ideas and rests each winning idea for at least a month before reposting it.

founders.summary: 84% of AI product answers named different brands the next day, and the top pick held its spot only 63% of the time.

founders.summary: Executives who copy a teammate on your email asking only who the right person is almost force that teammate to take the meeting.

founders.title: How to Write High Converting Personalized Copy with Claude
founders.summary: Words like “unlock” and “elevate” now mark copy as AI-written, so give the model real details like the price before it drafts anything.

founders.title: How Not to Light Money on Fire Sponsoring Tech Events
founders.summary: Tech event sponsors should focus on providing high-caliber value to attract significant leads like founders and VCs.

founders.title: KeyBanc's 2026 AI x Software Survey: 24% Median ARR Growth, Only 6% at the Rule of 40, and 43% of Vendors Watching Customers Vibe Code Their Product
founders.summary: KeyBanc's 2026 survey reveals B2B software companies growing median ARR by 24% in 2025, with 43% of vendors observing customers using AI to recreate products.

crypto.title: Kraken Parent Payward Acquires Tribe Capital to Enter Private Markets
crypto.summary: Payward, Kraken's parent, agreed to acquire Tribe Capital, a venture firm managing $2.7 billion chaired by Payward and Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi, with closing expected in Q1 2027 at an undisclosed price. The deal adds private-market investing to a vertical buildout that also includes the pending purchase of derivatives exchange Bitnomial, a $600 million acquisition of stablecoin payments firm Reap, and the buyout of Magic Labs' wallet business. Sethi's concurrent role as Tribe chair and Payward co-CEO positions the transaction as a formal consolidation of an already-integrated executive relationship rather than a standard external acquisition.

crypto.title: Ledger expands hardware hack investigation to Germany and UAE
crypto.summary: Ledger says new tampered devices in Berlin and Dubai are the same incident as the Southeast Asia campaign, with extra hardware that captures the recovery phrase during setup, and one case involves the newer Nano Gen5. It says there is no flaw in its chip or OS and no confirmed case from ledger.com. Two users claim a combined $604,000 in losses from a Dubai-authorized reseller, and Bitquery reports about $1.68M stolen from 16 wallets in Dubai and Berlin, after earlier claims of $102M from 335 wallets in Southeast Asia. Ledger has not confirmed loss amounts and expects more devices to surface.

crypto.title: Lightspark Launches Agent Accounts for AI Agents
crypto.summary: Lightspark announced Agent Accounts, dedicated financial accounts that give AI agents the ability to hold balances and transact autonomously across multiple payment rails and currencies. The product targets developers building agents that need native payment capabilities, positioning Lightspark's Lightning-based infrastructure as the broadest multi-method solution for agent-to-agent and agent-to-human payments.

crypto.title: Ant International launches protocol for real-time settlement
crypto.summary: The Whale Orchestration Protocol runs on Ant's WhaleRTP platform and enables delivery-versus-payment between tokenized deposits and tokenized money market funds, developed under MAS's BLOOM initiative. Pilots with DBS and Franklin Templeton are complete. Separately, MAS issued S$100M of tokenized MAS Bills on November 6, Standard Chartered expanded tokenized deposits across Singapore and Hong Kong, and StraitsX, OCBC, and Standard Chartered finished an interoperability trial.

crypto.title: The Everything-App Race: Stickiness, Rev-Sharing, and Cross-Margin
crypto.summary: Robinhood, Polymarket, Kalshi, Coinbase, Kraken, and Pump.fun are each expanding beyond their originating verticals, converging on a shared product surface spanning stocks, crypto spot, perps, prediction markets, and memecoins from divergent starting points across TradFi and crypto-native distribution. Three decisive factors: customer retention depth, rev-sharing structures that attract new users and retain whales, and cross-margin capability across the full product stack. No clear differentiation thesis has emerged.

crypto.title: Kalshi vs. Polymarket: Domain Experts Win
crypto.summary: Kalshi and Polymarket launched within months of each other, but Kalshi now posts roughly 4x the volume at 3x the valuation, with a $65B raise in talks versus Polymarket's unannounced $21B round. Kalshi's MIT math founders, with prior finance careers, sued the CFTC, won regulatory standing, then expanded into single-stock perps on 50+ companies, indices, and AI compute futures this year. Polymarket became a tab inside a memecoin application, sitting beside memecoins and perps, its standalone-exchange identity absorbed into a retail crypto product. Founder background drove the split: quant-finance founders built toward prediction markets as a regulated asset class, while operator-type founders built toward distribution as the product.

crypto.title: Why Bitcoin needs capital markets and how Stacks is building them
crypto.summary: Bitcoin lacks yield, credit, and trading markets, and holders shouldn't have to hand over BTC to earn. Stacks' Bitcoin staking is live, with bonds targeting 3% annual yield paid in BTC from miners' Proof of Transfer commitments. The first two bonds drew 735 BTC, with Bullish staking in Bond 3 and Anchorage offering custody. In 2027, Stacks plans an open auction through PoX-6 and borrowing stablecoins against staked BTC. STX is required at 5% of the BTC value, and SIP-034 raised block capacity up to 30x, with a 100x goal.

crypto.title: Morpho and Aave are in a full BD war
crypto.summary: Onchain lending now depends on distribution, partnerships, and integrations through neobanks, wallets, and exchanges, not just a good app. Morpho is plugging into apps people already use: Coinbase Borrow in New York, OKX Wallet on X Layer, earn products at Ledger, Bitso, Pulsar, Abra, and Deel, Robinhood Stock Tokens as collateral, and new APIs. Aave is pursuing infrastructure partners and new collateral through V4: Circle Mint, Privy, and Base for fintechs, Ethena Pay's Earn+, cirBTC, PAXGy, mWIN, and Coinbase tokenized stocks, plus the Avon acquisition for fixed-rate lending. V3 Core going blue-chip only pushes new assets to V4. The real race is owning tokenized non-crypto assets through early issuer partnerships, and most onchain lending will likely run on one of the two.

crypto.title: Hong Kong SFC adds Hyperliquid to its suspicious platforms alert list
crypto.summary: On November 18, the SFC added Hyperliquid and Hyperliquid Hong Kong to its “Suspicious Virtual Asset Trading Platforms” list.

crypto.title: Derpetual Launches Abstract Market Launcher Tool
crypto.summary: Derpetual launched the Abstract Market Launcher, a self-serve tool that lets users create peer-to-peer futures markets on any asset.

crypto.title: Europe regulated crypto, but can crypto businesses pay their bills?
crypto.summary: MiCA authorisation does not guarantee access to a fiat payment account, so even authorised, funded firms can struggle to pay staff, suppliers, and advisers.

crypto.title: How long it takes to empty a crypto card
crypto.summary: In checking withdrawal times by card, MetaMask takes no time to withdraw, ether.fi takes 10 seconds to an hour, Exa up to a minute, and Gnosis Pay 3 minutes with the card locked.

it.title: Palo Alto Networks strikes $4.5 billion deal for Applied Compute
it.summary: Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock, adding tools for training and serving customized open-weight AI models. The deal is expected to close in its fiscal third quarter of 2027 and will support deployments across public and sovereign clouds.

it.title: Microsoft and Intel deepen collaboration to deliver differentiated Azure infrastructure
it.summary: Microsoft and Intel have announced an expansion of their collaboration under a long-term agreement to advance Azure cloud and AI infrastructure. Microsoft will become the first company to use Intel Foundry's EMIB advanced packaging technology for its first-party silicon and secure multi-year Intel Xeon supply capacity, including the upcoming Diamond Rapids server CPUs. The partnership also covers system-level optimizations using CXL memory, Intel QuickAssist Technology, and Intel Trust Domain Extensions for confidential computing.

it.title: Workday creates European entity to govern sovereign cloud
it.summary: Workday plans to establish an Ireland-based company with an EU-citizen board to operate its EU Sovereign Cloud, keeping governance and operational decisions in Europe. The service runs on AWS European Sovereign Cloud, with the new entity and additional safeguards expected to become operational in early 2027.

it.title: Legacy software may be holding back enterprise AI
it.summary: Google Cloud's Jeanette Manfra argues that maintenance burdens and vendor lock-in are limiting organizations' AI ambitions. She cites Google-commissioned research in which 78% of surveyed technology leaders said maintaining legacy systems diverts resources from AI, and advocates greater vendor choice and stronger security requirements in procurement.

it.title: IT leaders are deciding which decisions machines can make on their own
it.summary: IT leaders and chief information officers are navigating the challenges of deploying autonomous IT and generative AI tools in high-security environments. While rules-based automation and large language models help synthesize large volumes of data and accelerate cybersecurity defenses, agencies face significant hurdles regarding data readiness, over-trust in AI results, and classifying sensitive information. Organizations are addressing these challenges by establishing localized large language models, data governance structures, and strict human-in-the-loop checkpoints.

it.title: Plaid built $382K in pipeline from one TLDR placement
it.summary: Close Q4 with proof. TLDR reaches 8 million tech readers across 14 newsletters. Book a Q4 campaign .

it.title: Nvidia expands Azure infrastructure and on-premises AI options
it.summary: Nvidia and Microsoft are expanding access to Azure virtual machines powered by Vera Rubin systems and adding more model customization capabilities through Microsoft Foundry. Planned Azure Local support for additional Nvidia GPUs and Jetson platforms will extend deployment options to on-premises and industrial environments.

it.title: OVHcloud announces 55 cloud and AI products
it.summary: OVHcloud unveiled 55 cloud and AI offerings spanning infrastructure, networking, development tools, and enterprise applications at its Paris summit. The announcements include plans to add Nvidia Blackwell B300 and Rubin R200 GPUs as the company expands its European-hosted services.

it.title: Sashiko: Lessons from building an agentic code review system for Linux
it.summary: Google's AI and Infrastructure team built Sashiko, an open-source, agentic code review system powered by Gemini designed to help maintainers review Linux kernel patches. The system separates bug finding from verification using parallel specialist sessions and per-bug deep checks. Data from seven months of production use on kernel mailing lists show that Sashiko completes about 1,200 reviews daily and correlates with a 35 percent drop in 60-day follow-up fixes for merged commits.

it.title: Introducing agent controls: An enterprise control plane for agent behavior
it.summary: Microsoft has introduced agent controls, a managed Azure service designed to help enterprises centrally define, manage, and evaluate policies governing AI agent behavior. Built on the open-source Agent Control Specification and Agent Hooks, the service brings runtime governance to heterogeneous AI agent fleets without requiring organizations to build custom policy infrastructure. It evaluates agent actions and content using content safety classifiers, LLM judges, and deterministic Rego rules.

it.title: Enterprise AI needs more than GPUs
it.summary: AI agents also need CPUs, networking, storage, and isolated environments to execute code and interact with enterprise systems.

it.title: Amazon CloudFront Functions now supports network calls
it.summary: Amazon CloudFront Functions now supports network calls, allowing lightweight JavaScript running at edge locations to make API requests and act on the responses in real time.

hardware.title: Unsloth Desktop now runs on your NPU: 100+ agentic apps on AMD Ryzen™ AI
hardware.summary: AMD XDNA™ 2 NPUs are the world's first NPUs supported by Unsloth Desktop, the app for running AI models locally on your PC. Connect Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Cline, VS Code, Open WebUI and 100+ more agentic apps through the Unsloth API. GPU stays free: Your Radeon™ GPU keeps gaming, rendering or editing (memory permitting). Unplug: Power-efficient NPU inference can help extend battery life. Local by design: Models run on your PC. One-click setup: Install Unsloth, enable NPU (~47 MB, one time). Supported on Ryzen™ AI 300, 400 and Max Series processors, including PRO models. Windows 11 or Linux. Read the blog →

hardware.title: Google books a dedicated New Glenn launch in Q1 2029 for Project Suncatcher, its orbital TPU compute constellation
hardware.summary: Each Suncatcher satellite carries roughly a data center rack's worth of computing and runs on solar power in sun-synchronous orbit, forming an interconnected network of TPUs for machine learning compute. The mission is Google's first dedicated heavy-lift launch for the project, using New Glenn's large payload volume. The booking is for 2029 even though New Glenn's hotfire anomaly investigation is still ongoing.

hardware.title: OpenAI's models rewrite RTL for up to 14% PPA gains on AMD's flagship GPU IP and 10 to 13% smaller blocks on its Jalapeño chip
hardware.summary: The models rewrote SystemVerilog for AMD's already-optimized GPU blocks, with some changes in a design sent for manufacturing and single-digit gains verified on its next flagship CPU. On Jalapeño, the matrix and SIMD blocks shrank 10% to 13%, confirmed in silicon, partly by rewriting adders and multipliers, including a multiplier cut from two cycles to one. OpenAI is also training GPT-Synopsys with Synopsys to drive EDA tools directly.

hardware.title: Relativity finishes Terran R second-stage testing and interstage structural qualification as stage one integration nears completion
hardware.summary: The second stage hot-fired at NASA Stennis's A2 stand, and the interstage passed structural testing on Long Beach's “Tender Loving Crusher” rig. The thrust structure, housing all 13 Aeon R engines, fluid lines, and avionics, is being mated to stage one. At LC-16, the launch table framing is done and a second pad lift cylinder has arrived. Relativity still targets a late 2026 debut, though observers expect 2027.

hardware.title: Detachable fiber connectors are emerging for CPO and NPO because standard fibers can't be reworked, tray-handled, or tested at volume
hardware.summary: Fibers bonded to photonic chips can't be reworked if one breaks, dangle during pick-and-place, and eat die-edge shoreline, since 125 µm cladding adds up across 16 fibers. Designs now bring light out at the edge or through a 45° mirror, with lenses, snap-fit alignment, or magnets replacing active alignment. Senko and Advantest demonstrated a test connector surviving 10,000 matings with little loss variation, but there's still no standard interface.

hardware.title: SHAPE trains a VLA on egocentric human video with discrete action tokens and two parallel action streams for a bimanual robot with 22-DoF hands
hardware.summary: Human video only gives retargeted end-effector actions, not the joint commands robots need. SHAPE's Qwen3-VL-4B backbone predicts discrete EEF action tokens as an auxiliary task, while a shared flow-matching expert outputs separate EEF and joint streams. Joint readout scores 0.80 across six tasks versus 0.63 for π0.5, and EEF readout via IK transfers better from humans. After human-data pretraining, it learns new tasks from human demos with no task-specific robot data.

hardware.title: A 3D-printed, electronics-free soft hexapod hits 4.72 m/s by reusing compressed air like a compound steam engine
hardware.summary: Higher air pressure speeds up a pneumatic robot but wastes energy, so the team routes air through small high-pressure chambers that power the valves, then through larger low-pressure chambers that move the legs, as in a compound steam engine. The six-legged robot is printed in one piece from one soft material and runs about 100 times faster than the 2022 version, over sand, mulch, and concrete, and in water. It's still tethered to an air compressor.

hardware.title: California's attorney general subpoenas Nvidia over whether advanced chips or confidential information reached China
hardware.summary: AG Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena asking whether Nvidia's chips or confidential data ended up in China, and whether Nvidia misled investors about that risk under California securities law. The probe follows Jensen Huang's resignation and centers on Megaspeed, the Singapore data center operator suspected of diverting restricted chips, plus how Nvidia reports overseas revenue. Nvidia's market value has dropped over $1 trillion in two weeks, and it hasn't commented yet.

hardware.title: Meta reportedly prices its pocket-sized Muse Charm at $300 with a free year of Verizon 5G, delaying its smartwatch to 2027
hardware.summary: Charm has a roughly 2-inch screen navigated with a thumb and a customizable Muse character at its center, and it carries the Muse AI agent into the real world. The bundled 5G data, up to 12 months from Verizon, is meant to speed Muse's responses away from Wi-Fi. Meta plans a December launch and pushed its smartwatch to 2027 to make room, and it didn't deny the pricing report.

hardware.title: Fabs can use AI to search huge recipe spaces and flag defects, but autonomous process control is blocked by data gaps, agent governance, and the cost of requalifying models that keep learning
hardware.summary: AI found better etch recipes in months where a year of manual work stalled, but each of the thousands of candidates still needs an expensive silicon experiment to validate.

hardware.title: BepiColombo's MIXS delivers its first X-ray images after eight years in transit, ahead of Mercury orbit insertion on November 21
hardware.summary: The Leicester-built Mercury Imaging X-ray Spectrometer imaged one of the sky's brightest X-ray sources as a calibration test.

hardware.title: Sophia Space's orbital OS self-deploys across Kepler relay satellites using Kubernetes and triple redundancy
hardware.summary: An alpha of SOOS copied itself across three of four Jetson Orin processors on one Kepler satellite, then hopped the optical link to a second satellite and repeated, with managed Kubernetes spreading jobs between spacecraft.

hardware.title: IEA says datacenter electricity use doubles by 2030 while US gas and Chinese coal push emissions up 70%
hardware.summary: The IEA projects data centers going from about 120 GW today to roughly 1,000 TWh a year by 2030.
